heading: Subcontracting
previous_text: The vendor shall not subcontract any part of this engagement without the client's prior written consent.
current_text: The vendor may subcontract any part of this engagement at its sole discretion.
reason: Client's approval right over subcontracting removed entirely.
policy_rule: Subcontracting requires the client's prior written consent

heading: Liability
previous_text: The vendor's total liability shall not exceed the total fees paid in the preceding 12 months.
current_text: The vendor's liability shall be unlimited.
reason: Liability cap removed entirely.
policy_rule: Liability cap must not exceed 12 months of contract value

heading: Force Majeure
previous_text: Neither party shall be liable for delays caused by events beyond their reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, or government action.
current_text: Neither party shall be liable for delays caused by events beyond their reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, government action, or vendor staffing shortages.
reason: Force majeure scope broadened to cover vendor's own staffing issues, reducing vendor accountability.
policy_rule: Force majeure must not cover a party's own operational or staffing failures

heading: Confidentiality
previous_text: Both parties shall maintain confidentiality for a period of 5 years following termination.
current_text: Both parties shall maintain confidentiality for a period of 1 year following termination.
reason: Confidentiality period drastically shortened.
policy_rule: Confidentiality obligations must survive at least 3 years post-termination

heading: Termination
previous_text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 60 days written notice.
current_text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 45 days written notice.
reason: Notice period shortened but still reasonable.
policy_rule: Termination notice period must not be less than 30 days

heading: Dispute Resolution
previous_text: Any dispute arising under this agreement shall first be resolved through good-faith negotiation, followed by binding arbitration if unresolved within 30 days.
current_text: Any dispute arising under this agreement shall be resolved solely through litigation in the vendor's chosen jurisdiction.
reason: Arbitration path removed, forcing costly litigation in vendor-favored jurisdiction.
policy_rule: Dispute resolution must include a mandatory arbitration step before litigation

heading: Data Protection
previous_text: The vendor shall implement industry-standard data protection measures and comply with applicable data privacy laws.
current_text: The vendor shall implement reasonable data protection measures where feasible.
reason: Data protection obligation weakened from mandatory to discretionary.
policy_rule: Data protection measures must be mandatory, not discretionary
